name: Guillem Figueira
dates: fl. first half of the 13th century
bio: Guillem Figueira was of Toulouse, the son of a tailor and himself a tailor. After the French took Toulouse he settled in Lombardy, and the sirvente of his given here is directed against Rome.

The verse in this selection is Ida Farnell's English version in The Lives of the Troubadours (London: David Nutt, 1896), where it stands beside a prose Life of the poet; the prose Life is not reproduced here. The dates are those Farnell prints for the period in which the poet was active, and the Old Occitan original is not included.

poems.title: Three Stanzas of the Sirvente on Rome
poems.author: Guillem Figueira
poems.text:
Lo, a song I sing
With melody that pleases,
Hence vain dallying,
Since speech my bosom eases.
Him that thus would sing
I wot swift vengeance seizes;
Nathless I will rise
'Gainst that Head of lies,
Rome, whom all despise,
Foul source of all diseases
Whereof virtue dies.

Rome, deceiver dread,
Who gold alone reverest,
From thy sheep unfed
Full close the wool thou shearest.
He, whose blood was shed,
And to mankind is dearest,
He whom now I seek
Break thy rav'nous beak.
Rome, as traitress sleek
And liar thou appearest
To Latin and to Greek.

Rome, on flesh of weak
And foolish men thou feedest,
Blind ones guidance seek.
Whom in the ditch thou leadest;
God's commandment eke
Methinks thou little heedest;
Since by lust of gold
Pardons thou hast sold
Unto sinners bold;
Rome, great strength thou needest
Sin's burden to uphold.
